ALL FOUR of mc1l6's heads are this one wound, read by TWO different readers: the (10,42) castle PAINTER sub_285C0 raises 5 cells the port does not (heads t=11781 at site (12,24) and t=28754 at site (3,227)), and the castle-DEMOLISH walker sub_28FE0 razes those same 5 cells, whose per-cell wall arm draws the LCG -- so retail's collapse spends MORE draws and every downstream per-cell depth in the 35x35 rect shifts by a small signed amount (heads t=22561 and t=27826, 435 and 420 height cells apart in a single tick). (1) THE PORT IS BYTE-FAITHFUL: the goal decode was disassembled out of the shipped CARPET.EXE (sub_285C0 = file 0x40DB8; classify `cmp cl,0xf` at 0x288BD, the <0xF arm at 0x288C2, the >=0xF arm at 0x288E7 -- `cl % 16`, `(lo-1) << 2`, `+ target(z>>5)`, `- height`), and it matches the port's `fill_castle_goal_row` exactly; the inner-row rect geometry differs from the port's ONLY in the +4/+5 axis transposition, which is VACUOUS here because every castle course (build_tab rows 1..8) is SQUARE. (3) IT IS ROW 5 AND ONLY ROW 5: the take's five level-1..4 castle builds (t=2291/2386/2522/2580/2700/2774/.../11651) are BIT-EXACT on the height plane, and the collapse walker's draw count -- graded against RETAIL'S OWN LCG via pool slot 0's `+4` (MGC_COLLAPSE_PROBE) -- is EXACT for rows 4/3/2/1 (99/317/100/26) and SHORT for row 5 twice (port 895 v retail 899 at t=22560; port 864 v retail 869 at t=27814). (4) THE FIVE-BYTE SUBSTITUTION CLOSES THE TAKE: with MGC_BUILD_DAT_DAMAGE="12,24:2736=5B,2737=5F,2738=5F,2739=5F,2750=54" mc1l6 goes 5 segments / 4 excess resets / segmented horizon 11,780 -> 2 segments / 1 excess reset / horizon 28,753, BOTH collapse draw counts land on retail's exact 899 and 869, and cells (13,17)/(14,17)/(15,17)/(16,17) become bit-exact on height AND type AND angle; pointing the SAME five bytes at the other site ("3,227:...2750=57") closes head t=28754 instead. ⭐⭐⭐ FACTS ABOUT THE CLASS FROM THIS TAKE. ⚠⚠ THE 2026-09-09 AMENDMENT HERE WAS ITSELF WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN (round 159, dig w159j, re-measured and independently re-verified by the main session): it claimed 'the damage is PER-INSTANCE and CONSTANT IN TIME' and marked the dig's (b) REFUTED. The dig's (b) was RIGHT. The correct model is ONE level-wide in-memory image whose FOUR bytes 2736-2739 are CONSTANT across both sites and all three builds, while byte 2750 is RE-SCRIBBLED MID-RUN (low nibble 4 for the t=11733 build at site (12,24), 7 for the t=27748 build at the SAME site, 7 at site (3,227)). It is the SITE-INVARIANCE of the other four, not per-instance-ness, that is the strong evidence. DISCRIMINATOR (the graded lanes cannot see it — both models reach horizon END): with ONE value per site the UNGRADED height plane is wrong for 66 ticks from exactly t=27748 at cell (27,17) (`MGC_PLANE_DIFF=27000:39754` → `hdiff=1 [(27,17,52,53)]` climbing), while the two-phase image is `hdiff=0` on EVERY one of the 39,754 ticks. ⭐ A MEASURED `END` ON THE GRADED LANES DID NOT SETTLE THE MODEL; THE UNGRADED PLANE DID. Measured: the site-(12,24) fit closes EXACTLY heads 11781+22561+27826, and the site-(3,227) fit closes EXACTLY head 28754; the two are DISJOINT AND COMPLEMENTARY and together account for all four. What made it look time-varying is that MGC_BUILD_DAT_DAMAGE is SITE-SCOPED (one site per run), so no single invocation can close the take. The fit is also UNIQUE, not a best fit: a 16-value sweep of byte 2750 at site (12,24) yields horizon 28,753 for 0x54 and 11,797 for every other value. This makes the class PER-INSTANCE SELECTIVE, which is stronger evidence for data damage over a code defect than round 121's per-process argument. === WAVE 121 RE-CAUSATION (2026-09-08, digs D1 + D3, PLAYER-RULED: register the re-causation but KEEP status `open` -- bank the lead, excuse NOTHING) === THREE INDEPENDENT DIGS NOW TRIANGULATE ON CELL (25,103) AND POINT AT RETAIL-SIDE HEAP DAMAGE, NOT A PORT DEFECT. It also proved the build asset correct by cross-checking the bake against the UNCOMPRESSED shipped BUILD1-0.DAT (mc1-arctic), which agrees byte-for-byte over rows 1..45; cell (25,103)'s row-7 byte is 0x65 => goal 4*4+58 = 74, exactly like its neighbours. D1 then hit a WALL it could not pass: with h=58, goal=74, d=16 and divisor=15 IDENTICAL for (25,102), (25,103) and (25,104), retail raises the first and third and NOT the middle one -- 'logically impossible under the code I disassembled', and D1 said one of its three independently-confirmed facts had to be false. D3 also byte-verified the collapse walker sub_28FE0 (file 0x417d8) faithful and CRC-verified build.dat.bin against the RNC header's declared unpacked CRC (0x6522). (3) Round 120's own second witness cell (25,103) already recorded retail ending at type 76 while the port stamps type 22 -- the SAME cell and the SAME direction both later digs found independently. SCALE: 45 of mc1l48-nodeath's 62 live deviations are z-ONLY (73%, gating 15,141 ticks) and 32 of mc1l48's 51 (63%). STILL OPEN, and why this stays `open` rather than becoming `deviation`: D1's impossibility is RESOLVED by D3's damaged bytes but was not independently closed (nobody reconstructed retail's damaged in-memory row byte-by-byte), and D3 had NO mc1l49 control -- no take without the damage to show a clean level-7 demolish razing only the shipped cells. Excusing 45 boundaries on this would let a port defect pass certification if the read is wrong, so NOTHING is excused: this registration moves no horizon and no dev count. It banks the re-causation for the focused dig this rule already calls for.

RETAIL'S OWN BLIND WRITE, AND WHICH BINARY CAPTURED THE TAKE (round 163, 2026-09-23). `sub_25EC0`'s eruption handover makes TWO blind writes gated only on `slot != 0` (the `> pool base` pointer test at :28779 and :28791 — no class, no model, no life): the KICK stamps `+26 = 250` into whatever record now holds the previous erupting slot, and the PLUME soft-kill stamps `flags |= 0x400` (0x400 = 1024) into whatever inherited the previous plume's slot. Both sites are at the SAME VA in both MC1 builds — KICK VA 0x25FBE `66 c7 42 1a fa 00`, PLUME VA 0x26035 `call` → soft-kill 0x41E80 (CARPET) / 0x421C0 (HIDDEN). THIS RULE REGISTERS THE PLUME HALF. ⭐⭐⭐ WHY IT IS BIT-SCOPED AND NOT TICK-SCOPED: whether a recording carries these writes is a property of the BINARY THAT CAPTURED IT, not of the tick, the slot or the class. `tools/mc_exe_tickpatch.py --volcano-guard` (round 162, player-validated in-game 2026-09-21) installs the DOS-side half of the port's `volcano_register_revalidate` patch and emits `*_RECVG.EXE`; a take captured on that binary simply does not perform the blind write, and the faithful port arm does. So the SAME port code is correct against one recording and 1024 high against another, purely by capture provenance. A tick list would therefore have to be re-derived for every new take and would silently mis-grade any take whose binary was mis-remembered. `xor_mask: 1024` registers the CLASS once: the row matches only when `retail ^ port == 0x400` exactly — that one bit differs and no other, IN EITHER DIRECTION — so a guarded take (port sets the bit, retail does not) and an unguarded take (retail sets it, port does not, e.g. under the `MGC_REPLAY_VOLCANO_GUARD` probe) both grade clean, and no take needs to declare its binary. ⚙ PROVENANCE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, on the round-163 intake: mc1hwl8 was the ONLY take of the 18 with retail-side 0x400 rows (5) and no port-side rows — i.e. captured UNGUARDED — and every mc1hwl9-and-up take showed the port-side signature; the player independently confirmed that the guard did not exist when l8 was recorded and that l9+ were all played on the guarded binary. The two arms are otherwise identical, which is itself the corroboration. SCOPE: `flags` only, `xor_mask` 1024 only. The KICK half (`+26 = 250`) is NOT covered here — it is registered per take where it has been witnessed (`mc1l26-froze-level-250-castle-oob`, `mc1l45-froze-level-250-castle-oob`), because a 250 stamp is not a single bit and its downstream (an out-of-bounds downgrade ladder that HANGS retail) is far more than one row. Zero kick rows were measured in the round-163 corpus. ⚠ HONEST RESIDUAL: a genuine port defect that flips exactly bit 0x400 of `flags` and nothing else would be masked by this rule. That is the price of registering a bit rather than a tick; 0x400 is the narrowest bit that carries the deviation, and the runner's per-rule hit count is the watch on it (a count that jumps an order of magnitude is a signal, not a mask). ⭐ THE PLAYER'S STANDING LEAD, now corroborated: the blind writes land class-agnostically on arbitrary records and may be a substantial source of the campaign's unexplained OOB residue — when a deviation resists explanation, ask whether a volcano was erupting. ⚖ PLAYER-RULED 2026-09-23: *"we should have a registered deviation for the volcano stuff, so that it does not matter which recording is on the fixed binary and which not-fixed … we don't need to spend more time with the volcano overall."* ⭐⭐⭐ NARROWED THE SAME DAY, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED, NOT THEORETICAL: `xor_mask` ALONE WAS MASKING A REAL PORT DEFECT. `0x400` is not the volcano's bit, it is the GENERIC death/reap bit (`sub_41E80` = `+17 |= 4`), so the bit-only rule excused ANY death-flag-only divergence.
